title: WES Credential Evaluation for 3-Year Indian Degrees & GRE-Optional US Universities

runs.t: A three-year Indian bachelor's degree does not receive one universal admission decision across U.S. universities. Each university—and sometimes each graduate programme—sets its own credential requirements. A WES evaluation can help explain the academic credential, but it does not override the university's admission policy or guarantee eligibility.

Before paying for a credential evaluation, check the exact programme's international admission rules. Some U.S. institutions consider qualifying three-year Indian degrees under specified conditions; others require a four-year equivalent or additional study.

sections.title: What is a WES credential evaluation?

runs.t: World Education Services (WES) provides credential evaluations that compare academic qualifications earned outside the United States with U.S. education standards. Universities may request an evaluation, but the U.S. does not have one government agency that decides all international academic equivalencies.

A university may require WES, accept another NACES-member evaluator, conduct its own assessment or ask for documents directly. Follow the university's instructions rather than ordering an evaluation simply because it is commonly discussed online.

sections.title: How does WES assess a three-year Indian bachelor's degree?

runs.t: WES's published guidance states that it considers certain three-year Indian bachelor's degrees equivalent to a four-year U.S. bachelor's degree when the degree is awarded in First Division by a university accredited by NAAC with Grade A or better. Students must check the current WES policy and the specific institution's eligibility requirements.

A WES equivalency is an evaluation opinion. It is not an admission decision. A graduate school may still consider the subject, grades, institution, prerequisites, professional experience and programme-specific requirements.

sections.title: What if your degree is not accepted as equivalent?

runs.t: Ask the graduate admissions office whether a three-year degree plus additional postgraduate study can meet the entry requirement.
Check whether the programme offers a bridge or pathway option.
Ask whether the university accepts a particular credential evaluator and what report type it requires.
Do not assume a postgraduate diploma, professional certificate or work experience will automatically replace the missing academic requirement.
Keep written confirmation from the admissions office for the exact programme and intake.

sections.title: GRE-optional universities: what does test-optional mean?

runs.t: GRE policies are set by universities and often by individual departments. A university may be test-optional for one programme and require GRE scores for another. Some departments may accept scores but not require them; others may recommend them for applicants with a particular academic profile.
Check the programme's official admissions page for the intake you plan to join.
Confirm whether GRE is required, optional, recommended or not accepted.
Check whether a waiver is automatic or must be requested.
Review whether the programme requires other tests, portfolios, prerequisite courses or work experience.
Do not assume that a university-wide GRE policy applies to every graduate programme.

sections.title: What to prepare before contacting admissions

runs.t: Exact degree title, awarding university and affiliated college, if applicable.
Degree duration, year of award, division/class and grading scale.
NAAC accreditation grade and validity information relevant to the awarding institution.
Official transcripts, consolidated marksheets and degree certificate.
Details of additional postgraduate study, if any.
Target programme, intake and link to the published admission requirements.

faq.q: Do all U.S. universities accept three-year Indian bachelor's degrees?

runs.t: No. Policies vary by university and programme. Some consider qualifying degrees under specific conditions, while others require a four-year equivalent or additional study.

faq.q: Does a WES report guarantee admission to a U.S. master's programme?

runs.t: No. WES evaluates credentials; the university makes the admission decision and may apply additional programme requirements.

faq.q: Does WES accept three-year Indian degrees?

runs.t: WES publishes criteria under which certain three-year Indian bachelor's degrees may be evaluated as equivalent to a four-year U.S. bachelor's degree. Check the latest WES policy and document requirements.

faq.q: Are GRE scores optional at all U.S. universities?

runs.t: No. GRE policies vary by institution, department, programme and intake. Check the official programme page.

faq.q: Should I get WES evaluation before applying?

runs.t: Only if the university or programme requires it, or if you have confirmed it will be useful for your application. Follow the institution's specified evaluator and report type.
